question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $-\dfrac{3}{2}=\dfrac{(-3)}{2}.$

To raise the fraction to the power of $3$, we must raise both the numerator and the denominator to the power of $3\mathbin{:}$

$$
\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^3=\left(\dfrac{(-3)}{2}\right)^3=\dfrac{(-3)^3}{2^3}
$$

Now, computing $(-3)^3=-27$ and $2^3=8,$ we get

$$
\dfrac{(-3)^3}{2^3}= \dfrac{-27}{8}=-\dfrac{27}{8} .
$$
